widgets_values:
# MV H3

Song + isolated vocal + one photo → finished music video, joined and muxed.
No ffmpeg.

Output: `output/minimax_h3_t8_long_video/<chain_id>/assembled/*_master_audio.mp4`

Full docs, model download links and the Claude Code skill:
**github.com/oomsurvivor/comfyui-mv-autodirect**

---

**Vocal must be the isolated lead stem.** Backing vocals count as singing and
break the timing.

**Both `AudioCrop` nodes need the same `start_time` / `end_time`**, and
`end_time` at least 1 second shorter than the shorter file. Otherwise:
`resolves to N frames but requires M`.

## Three ways to run

| | |
|---|---|
| **Preview** | Ctrl+B on the renderer → Run → read `PreviewAny`. **No GPU, near-instant.** Change `seed` and repeat until the plan looks right. |
| **Excerpt** | change `end_time` on **both** AudioCrops + new `chain_id` |
| **Full song** | `0:00` → length minus 1–2 s + new `chain_id` |

Short runs cost *more* per scene — the model reloads for every scene and that
fixed cost is spread over fewer of them. Iterate with Preview, not with short
renders.

## chain_id — the one real trap

Reusing a **finished** `chain_id` generates nothing and re-exports the old
video in a second, with no error. Signs: no `100%|███ 6/6` bar, GPU quiet.

**New look → new chain_id.**

## Extra reference inputs

Down the left edge, seventeen loaders are already wired to the renderer through
`Set`/`Get` pairs: **8 images, 3 videos with their soundtracks, 3 audios**.

They ship **bypassed** (pale). To use one: click it, press **Ctrl+B**, pick the
file. Leave the rest bypassed - a bypassed loader sends nothing and the slot is
simply ignored.

A reference does nothing until the prompt names it. Write the tag in
`custom_global_prompt`:

> the woman in `<Picture 1>` holding the flute from `<Picture 2>`

`<Picture 1>` is the main image; `<Picture 2>`…`<Picture 9>` are the extra ones,
in order. Same for `<Video 1..3>` and `<Audio 1..3>`.

## The four fields on MV Auto Director

In the order they appear: `custom_global_prompt` (required) ·
`custom_angles_json` · `custom_light` · `custom_pose`

Describe crowds in the **global** field only — it is not word-filtered, the
angle library is. Lock the light to a fixed world position so cuts don't
flicker.

`busy_background`: leave on `auto`. It avoids pairing expensive moves with wide
shots, which can take roughly ten times as long.

`pose_scenes` / `pose_every` make scenes stop lip-syncing. A third is a good
rhythm; put them at the intro, a breakdown, and after a chorus payoff.

## Notes

`accepted/` means the file landed, not that the frame is good. Check for a
duplicated face or a second ball — a bad scene poisons every scene after it.

Closing the **console** kills the server; closing the **browser tab** does not.

widgets_values:
## Multiple references

Up to **9 images, 3 videos, 3 audios** — the stock renderer allows only one.

A reference does nothing until the prompt names it:

| Tag | Points to |
|---|---|
| `<Picture 1>` | `reference_image` |
| `<Picture 2>`…`<Picture 9>` | `ref_image_2…9` |
| `<Video 1..3>` · `<Audio 1..3>` | video / audio refs |

Write the tags in **`custom_global_prompt`**:

> the man in `<Picture 1>` wearing the jacket from `<Picture 2>`

That splits face / outfit / location into separate images.

**Extra refs are not part of the resume contract.** Swapping one while keeping
the same `chain_id` silently reuses the old scenes — the `report` output prints
a fingerprint; when it changes, change `chain_id`.

More images of the *same* person means more consistency, not more variety. Tags
are fixed for the whole chain, so one chain is one outfit.

Reference video: at least 5 frames, truncated to the scene length.
